title: Large-Scale Study of GitHub Copilot Trajectories
abstract: arXiv:2610.32313v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI coding agents are increasingly integrated into software development workflows. However, most coding agent studies rely on benchmarks similar to SWE-bench, which assume autonomous agents operating in a single trajectory. This assumption does not mirror real-world usage, where developers interactively collaborate with agents. We address this gap by studying human-in-the-loop agent trajectories in the wild, focusing on 7,581 Copilot-authored PRs with publicly accessible session data. We find that 58% of Copilot PRs have no human intervention, and that when developers do intervene, collaboration is brief (median of 2 Human-AI loops). Merged PRs also tend to have fewer initial trajectory iterations than unmerged ones. We also find that the trajectory following the first human intervention exhibits a significant drop of 20.8 iterations and 8.4 min in duration. However, trajectories following later interventions show minimal iteration drops

translated_title: GitHub Copilot 智能体轨迹的大规模研究
translated_abstract: AI 编程智能体正日益融入软件开发工作流。然而，大多数编程智能体研究依赖于类似 SWE-bench 的基准测试，这些测试假设智能体在单一轨迹中自主运行。这一假设无法反映真实世界中的使用情况，即开发者与智能体进行交互式协作。我们通过研究真实环境中人在回路的智能体轨迹来填补这一空白，重点分析了 7,581 个由 Copilot 撰写且具有公开可访问会话数据的 PR。我们发现，58% 的 Copilot PR 没有任何人类干预，而当开发者确实介入时，协作是短暂的（人机循环中位数为 2 次）。已合并的 PR 的初始轨迹迭代次数也往往少于未合并的 PR。我们还发现，第一次人类干预之后的轨迹在迭代次数上显著下降 20.8 次，持续时间缩短 8.4 分钟；然而，后续干预之后的轨迹迭代次数下降幅度则很小。
tldr: 该研究通过分析 7,581 个真实 GitHub Copilot 智能体 PR 的人在回路轨迹，揭示了真实开发中人与 AI 智能体的协作模式——大多数 PR 无人类干预且协作短暂，而首次人类干预会显著缩短后续轨迹，弥补了现有基准测试假设与真实使用场景之间的差距。
en_tdlr: This large-scale study of 7,581 real-world GitHub Copilot agent-authored PRs reveals human-in-the-loop collaboration patterns in the wild, showing that 58% of PRs involve no human intervention and that the first human intervention significantly shortens subsequent agent trajectories.
